speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of chronic joint pain. To begin my assessment, can you describe exactly where you are feeling this pain and how long you have been experiencing it?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest is classic for osteoarthritis; however, I need to know if you have experienced any swelling, warmth, or redness in those joints, specifically your left great toe.

REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray_left_great_toe, X-ray_hips, X-ray_knees.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteoarthritis. The normal inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) and the mechanical nature of your pain—worsening with activity and improving with rest—are highly specific for degenerative joint disease rather than inflammatory arthritis or infection. Given your age and the involvement of the great toe, hips, and knees, this is likely polyarticular osteoarthritis.
